column1: To eke out a full-time living from their honeybees, about half the nation’s 2,000 commercial beekeepers pull up stakes each spring, migrating north to find more flowers for their bees.
column2: 为了依靠养蜂维持全职生活，大约一半的2000名商业养蜂人每年春天都会放弃原有居所，向北迁徙以寻找更多花源供蜜蜂采蜜。

column1: Besides turning floral nectar into honey, these hardworking insects also pollinate crops for farmers -for a fee.
column2: 除了将花蜜转化为蜂蜜，这些勤劳的昆虫还为农民提供授粉服务，并收取费用。

column1: As autumn approaches, the beekeepers pack up their hives and go south, scrambling for pollination contracts in hot spots like California’s fertile Central Valley.
column2: 随着秋天的到来，养蜂人会收拾蜂箱，南下寻找授粉合同，尤其是在像加州肥沃的中央谷地这样的热点地区。

column1: Of the 2,000 commercial beekeepers in the United States about half migrate.
column2: 在美国，大约有2000名商业养蜂人，其中约一半会迁徙。

column1: This pays off in two ways.
column2: 这从两个方面带来了好处。

column1: Moving north in the summer and south in the winter lets bees work a longer blooming season, making more honey — money — for their keepers.
column2: 在夏季向北迁移、冬季向南迁移，可以让蜜蜂在更长的时间内持续开花，从而产出更多的蜂蜜，为蜂农带来更多的收益。

column1: Second, beekeepers can carry their hives to farmers who need bees to pollinate their crops.
column2: 其次，养蜂人可以将蜂箱运送到需要授粉的农民那里。

column1: Every spring a migratory beekeeper in California may move up to 160 million bees to flowering fields in Minnesota and every winter his family may haul the hives back to California, where farmers will rent the bees to pollinate almond and cherry trees.
column2: 每年春天，一位来自加利福尼亚的迁徙养蜂人都会将多达1.6亿只蜜蜂带到明尼苏达州的开花田野中。而到了冬天，他会把蜂箱运回加利福尼亚，那里的农民会租用这些蜜蜂来为杏仁树和樱桃树授粉。

column1: Migratory beekeeping is nothing new.
column2: 迁徙式养蜂其实并不是什么新鲜事物。

column1: The ancient Egyptians moved clay hives, probably on rafts, down the Nile to follow the bloom and nectar flow as it moved toward Cairo.
column2: 古埃及人可能将黏土蜂箱用筏子运下尼罗河，以追随花期和蜜源向开罗方向的流动。

column1: In the 1880s North American beekeepers experimented with the same idea, moving bees on barges along the Mississippi and on waterways in Florida, but their lighter, wooden hives kept falling into the water.
column2: 在19世纪80年代，北美的养蜂人尝试了类似的方案，他们用驳船将蜜蜂运送到密西西比河以及佛罗里达州的水道中。不过，那些较轻的木制蜂箱常常会掉进水中。

column1: Other keepers tried the railroad and horse-drawn wagons, but that didn’t prove practical.
column2: 其他养蜂人尝试了铁路和马车运输，但这种方法并不实用。

column1: Not until the 1920s when cars and trucks became affordable and roads improved, did migratory beekeeping begin to catch on.
column2: 直到20世纪20年代汽车和卡车变得负担得起、道路条件改善之后，迁徙式养蜂才开始流行。

column1: For the Californian beekeeper, the pollination season begins in February.
column2: 对于加利福尼亚州的养蜂人来说，授粉季节从二月开始。

column1: At this time, the beehives are in particular demand by farmers who have almond groves; they need two hives an acre.
column2: 此时，拥有杏仁种植园的农民对蜂箱需求特别大，每英亩需要两箱。

column1: For the three-week long bloom, beekeepers can hire out their hives for $32 each.
column2: 在持续三周的开花期，养蜂人可以将蜂箱出租，每箱租金为32美元。

column1: It’s a bonanza for the bees too.
column2: 对蜜蜂来说，这也是个大好机会。

column1: Most people consider almond honey too bitter to eat so the bees get to keep it for themselves.
column2: 大多数人认为杏仁蜂蜜太苦，不适合食用，因此蜜蜂可以自行保留这种蜂蜜享用。

column1: By early March it is time to move the bees.
column2: 到三月初，该移动蜂群了。

column1: It can take up to seven nights to pack the 4,000 or so hives that a beekeeper may own.
column2: 要整理一个养蜂人拥有的大约4000个蜂箱，可能需要长达七个夜晚的时间。

column1: These are not moved in the middle of the day because too many of the bees would end up homeless.
column2: 这些蜂巢不会在白天被移动，因为那样做会导致太多蜜蜂失去家园。

column1: But at night, the hives are stacked onto wooden pallets, back-to-back in sets of four, and lifted onto a truck.
column2: 但到了晚上，蜂箱会被堆叠在木制托盘上，四箱背靠背地排列在一起，然后被抬上卡车。

column1: It is not necessary to wear gloves or a beekeeper’s veil because the hives are not being opened and the bees should remain relatively quiet.
column2: 由于蜂箱没有被打开，且蜜蜂处于相对安静的状态，因此无需佩戴手套或蜂农专用面罩。

column1: Just in case some are still lively, bees can be pacified with a few puffs of smoke blown into each hive’s narrow entrance.
column2: 为防止个别蜜蜂仍较活跃，可向每个蜂箱狭窄的入口处吹入几口烟雾以使其平静。

column1: In their new location, the beekeeper will pay the farmer to allow his bees to feed in such places as orange groves.
column2: 在新地点，养蜂人会向农民支付费用，让蜜蜂在柑橘园等地方采食。

column1: The honey produced here is fragrant and sweet and can be sold by the beekeepers.
column2: 这里生产的蜂蜜香气浓郁、味道甜美，可以由养蜂人出售。

column1: To encourage the bees to produce as much honey as possible during this period, the beekeepers open the hives and stack extra boxes called supers on top.
column2: 为了鼓励蜜蜂在这段时间里生产更多的蜂蜜，养蜂人会打开蜂箱，并在上面堆放一些额外的箱子。

column1: These temporary hive extensions contain frames of empty comb for the bees to fill with honey.
column2: 这些临时蜂房扩展部分包含供蜜蜂填满蜂蜜的空蜂框。

column1: In the brood chamber below, the bees will stash honey to eat later.
column2: 在下方的蜂巢中，蜜蜂会储存蜂蜜，以便日后食用。

column1: To prevent the queen from crawling up to the top and laying eggs, a screen can be inserted between the brood chamber and the supers.
column2: 为了防止蜂王爬到顶部并产卵，可以在育雏室和超级巢箱之间安装一个屏障。

column1: Three weeks later the honey can be gathered.
column2: 三周后就可以采蜜了。

column1: Foul smelling chemicals are often used to irritate the bees and drive them down into the hive’s bottom boxes, leaving the honey-filled supers more or less bee free.
column2: 人们常常使用有恶臭的化学物质来刺激蜜蜂，使其坠落到蜂箱底部的空间里，从而让装满蜂蜜的蜂箱几乎无蜂。

column1: These can then be pulled off the hive.
column2: 然后可以将这些物品从蜂巢中取出来。

column1: They are heavy with honey and may weigh up to 90 pounds each.
column2: 它们满载着蜂蜜，每只重达90磅。

column1: The supers are taken to a warehouse.
column2: 那些蜂箱的盖板被运到仓库。

column1: In the extracting room, the frames are lilted out and lowered into an “uncapper” where rotating blades shave away the wax that covers each cell.
column2: 在提取室，蜂框被取出并放入一个‘去盖器’中，旋转刀片刮去覆盖每个蜂房的蜡盖。

column1: The uncapped frames are put in a carousel that sits on the bottom of a large stainless steel drum.
column2: 未封盖的蜂框被放入一个安装在大型不锈钢鼓状容器底部的转盘上。

column1: The carousel is filled to capacity with 72 frames.
column2: 转盘装满了72个蜂框。

column1: A switch is flipped and the frames begin to whirl at 300 revolutions per minute; centrifugal force throws the honey out of the combs.
column2: 开关被翻转后，蜂框以每分钟300转的速度开始旋转，离心力将蜂蜜从蜂巢框中甩出。

column1: Finally, the honey is poured into barrels for shipment.
column2: 最后，蜂蜜被倒入桶中用于运输。

column1: After this, approximately a quarter of the hives weakened by disease, mites, or an ageing or dead queen, will have to be replaced.
column2: 此后，大约有四分之一的蜂箱因疾病、螨虫侵害，或蜂王老化或死亡而需被更换。

column1: To create new colonies, a healthy double hive, teeming with bees, can be separated into two boxes.
column2: 要创建新的蜂群，可以将一个健康的、充满蜜蜂的双框蜂箱分割成两个独立的蜂箱。

column1: One-half will hold the queen and a young, already mated queen can be put in the other half, to make two hives from one.
column2: 一半蜂箱用于容纳蜂王，另一半可放入一只已交配的年轻蜂王，从而将一个蜂箱改造为两个独立的蜂箱。

column1: By the time the flowers bloom, the new queens will be laying eggs, filling each hive with young worker bees.
column2: 当花朵盛开时，新蜂后开始产卵，使每个蜂巢充满年轻的工蜂。

column1: The beekeeper’s family will then migrate with them to their summer location.
column2: 养蜂人一家将随之迁往夏季地点。
